decisions.reason: Online support means service through digital channels, not a guarantee of a human agent. Shopify describes chatbot, live-agent, email and other digital channels. Payment-page example and Chinese align.
Customer-support scope is explicit and distinct from a transport ticket. Zendesk establishes support tickets and identifying numbers; request to include that identifier is natural.

Cambridge explicitly gives withdraw a complaint and the irregular withdrew/withdrawn forms. Possessive her in the original sentence is a normal use of the same verb phrase; no policy effects are asserted.
Post Office distinguishes lost, delayed and damaged mail. The courier investigation example teaches actual loss without treating a delay as proved loss.
Royal Mail directly uses redelivery and redeliveries for a further delivery attempt following missed delivery. The invented scheduled-day example is natural and claims no universal free service.
Google Voice explicitly distinguishes missed or dropped calls. The meaning is an unintentionally interrupted call and the return-call sentence fits it; no missed-call synonym is added.
Cambridge authenticates detailed specifications, commonly plural. Product dimensions/materials/performance and the shelf-fitting example align; no dimensions are invented as product facts.
Cambridge BOGO and BBC Learning English establish the retail expression. Eligible products/qualifying promotion scope is retained; the notebook sign is an original plausible scenario.

Tesco’s own spend-and-save promotion directly demonstrates threshold spending followed by a reduction. The definition does not teach all discounts as threshold offers or claim the historic promotion is current.
DHL’s actual glossary explicitly defines delivery of one order in multiple shipments. The missing-item example and Chinese splitting into batches match that stated sense.
Boots explicitly markets trial-size shampoo/conditioner items in a paid trial set. The definition correctly avoids equating trial-size with free samples or all travel-size products.

Cambridge authenticates without first asking for reasons/explanations. The entry correctly allows separate time/item conditions; the fourteen-day shop example is an invented particular policy, not statutory advice.
Cambridge explicitly includes tamper-evident seals/packaging showing whether opened or changed. Visible evidence is distinguished from impossible-to-open packaging, and torn seal example fits.
Apple’s own refurbishment page lists testing, inspection, cleaning and replacement as needed. New definition is appropriately general about variable scope and distinguishes refurbished from new.
Cambridge’s payment/restaurant bill sense supports the compositional request. Combining the bill is explicitly separated from equal splitting or one person ultimately paying every share.
NHS food-label page explicitly says naturally occurring sugar can remain in no-added-sugar products. The fruit-juice example matches this distinction without equating the phrase to sugar-free.
The NHS institutional page directly uses dietary restrictions. General limits due to health/religion/other reasons are semantically appropriate; it is not treated as synonymous only with allergy.
Cambridge gives spill liquids outside a container and both spilled/spilt forms. The moving-bus/my-drink example is a normal instance of the same phrase and the Chinese preserves near-spill.
Cambridge authenticates dead equipment as not working. Electrical outlet is explicit, and laptop battery reliance is a plausible result without repair instructions.
Cadent’s primary report explicitly uses smell of gas in a reported gas-escape context. The entry describes an odor resembling domestic fuel gas; it does not assert that every smell proves a leak.
Cambridge defines non-slip as designed to prevent sliding. A mat used under a mixing bowl is within scope, and the definition does not promise absolute slip prevention.
Merriam-Webster independently confirms sealable means capable of being sealed. IKEA provides a concrete bag example. The entry correctly does not require every sealable bag to be resealable.

Cambridge authenticates stuck as unable to move. The physical drawer/keys scenario and Chinese are consistent; inability to open is a valid narrower alias, not an invented synonym for a missing drawer.

aliasDecisions.term: refund to the original payment method
aliasDecisions.reason: 退回原支付方式 exactly matches the unchanged original-payment-method refund sense; it does not redirect payment to a new account.
派送失败 matches an unsuccessful delivery attempt in the unchanged target; it does not imply permanent parcel loss.
拆单 names the same action of splitting an order. The existing action body remains intact and is not merged with the separate shipment noun.
不加香菜 is the same dining request as the unchanged no-coriander expression; no allergy claim is added.

method: Independent actual reading of all final EN/ZH, POS, numbered meaning, aliases/forms and primary dictionary/institutional/retailer source content, including primary indexed text when direct Cambridge pages returned403. Every old alias target body and exact hash was separately checked. This is semantic/data approval, not a claim that build, search/browser or publication checks have run.
